article.title: The Community Garden Opens Its Gates
article.excerpt: Two years of digging, fundraising and Saturday mornings in the rain: the Foundry Lane garden is finally open to everyone.
article.bodyHtml:
A shared place to grow

The gates opened at ten. By half past, every raised bed had a family around it, the tool shed had a queue, and somebody had already claimed the sunny corner by the wall for tomatoes.

The Foundry Lane garden has been two years in the making. It began as a patch of rubble behind the old ironworks, offered to us on a peppercorn lease after the Winter Fair of 2028, and it has been built almost entirely by volunteer weekends since: twenty-two raised beds, a wheelchair-accessible path, a rainwater store, and a greenhouse pieced together from three donated ones.

I have lived on this street forty years and never once stood on this ground. Now my grandchildren grow beans here.

What happens next

This season

The beds are allocated, but the garden is not finished, and it is not meant to be. The growers' committee has three priorities:

  • A covered seating area, so the garden works in the rain it will certainly get
  • Weekly sessions with the youth club, growing the salads the kitchen crew cook with
  • A seed library in the old gatehouse, free to any Alderford household

Open every day

The gate is unlocked from eight until dusk. Tools live in the shed by the greenhouse, and the kettle is always on in the gatehouse on a Saturday morning.

If you can lay a slab, mend a frame or simply keep a kettle going, the volunteer team would love to hear from you. And if you just want somewhere green to sit, the gate is open every day until dusk.

Thank you

To the eighty-one people who gave to the garden appeal, the six local firms who lent tools and time, and the council officers who said yes when it mattered: this one is yours as much as ours.

course.title: Junior Athletics
course.description: Weekly athletics for children aged 7 to 12, coached by qualified volunteers at the King's Park track.
course.aboutHtml:
What we do

Track and field fundamentals in a friendly, coached setting: warm-ups, drills, and a different discipline every week.

  • Sprints, relays and middle distance
  • Long jump, high jump and throws
  • A club mini-meet at the end of every term

What to bring

Trainers, a water bottle and a waterproof. Everything else, including spikes for the older group, is provided.
